To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

inter-residue contacts, when used as a basis for scoring and analyzing protein docking models, are able to: (i) identify the native pose in a set of models; (ii) rank docking poses in order of similarity to the native structure; (iii) detect the correct docking orientation; (iv) identify the correct binding site; and (v) provide a useful tool for the analysis and design of protein-protein inhibitors.
the analysis of inter-residue and inter-molecular contacts, as represented by the corresponding maps, is a powerful approach to analyze and rank docking poses.

inter-residue contacts are a powerful tool for the analysis of both the three-dimensional structure and the binding mode of a protein complex; that the visualization of inter-residue contact information in inter-molecular maps can help in the interpretation and analysis of protein-protein docking models; and that the use of inter-molecule contact maps can help in identifying the binding mode of an inhibitor targeting a protein-protein interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computational methods that allow to analyze the structural and energetic features of protein-protein complex models, and to rank them according to their reliability.
the development of computational methods to help in the analysis of protein-protein docking predictions, with particular emphasis on the scoring of docking models and on their visualization.
the development of computational methods for protein complex analysis and for the scoring and selection of protein docking models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods presented in this work are able to rank docking models according to their structural similarity with the native protein complex.

the analysis methods we developed can be successfully applied to the analysis of protein complexes, to the scoring of protein-protein docking models, and to the rational design of inhibitors of protein-proteins interactions.
our analysis tools are very useful for the analysis and ranking of protein-protein docking models, but that they should be used together with other tools and methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the analysis of protein-protein docking models, the use of inter-molecular contact map representations and the analysis of inter-residue contact patterns are useful and complementary approaches.
we developed methods for the analysis and the scoring of protein-protein docking models that are based on inter-residue contacts.

we have developed a set of tools to analyze protein-protein complexes, to score docking models, to visualize the results and, finally, to use these tools for the design of inhibitors of protein-proteins interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the correct docking pose is known, it can be reliably identified by the analysis of inter-residue contact patterns.
the use of inter-molecular contact map analysis can be very helpful in the analysis step of protein-protein docking, and in the rational drug design of protein-protein interaction inhibitors.
the inter-residue contacts can be used to analyze protein structures and to score protein docking models.
